_comment: EXT-63, arm 27 — 1 h, LV-2 + LV-4 + LV-5 with LV-1 DELIBERATELY OFF.
The inertness check, and a claim that needs testing rather than asserting.
THE CLAIM.  LV-1 (iono_seed_field_frame) has exactly ONE actuator on this path.  A
seed is a linearization point and the network solve is exactly invariant to it
(2026-08-01 theorem; arm 16 confirmed it empirically with the carry off).  Its only
measured effect came through the rx-CB inject gate, which thresholded the PREFIT
|value_abs - x_lin(cb)| and therefore depended on where the seed put x_lin(cb) via
initializeCodeBiases.  Card LV-4 RETIRED that test.  So with LV-4 armed, LV-1 should
have no channel left at all.
PREDICTION, STATED BEFORE THE RUN: this arm reproduces arm 23 (LV-1+2+4+5, 1 h:
settled mean 35.24, sd 4.69, end 32.68, 7182 folds, 124 erases) to within run-to-run
noise -- NOT bit-identical (the seed still moves x_lin, and every innovation is
formed against it, so the arithmetic differs at the ulp level and a near-null level
direction amplifies that), but with no systematic difference in level, folds or
erases.
IF IT DIFFERS MATERIALLY: LV-1 has a second actuator nobody has named, and finding
it matters more than the level numbers -- candidates are any other PREFIT-thresholded
consumer (the prefit census fuse, the admission screens) or a row set that depends on
the seed's magnitude.  Do not proceed with the stack until it is named.
IF IT MATCHES: LV-1 is INERT in the recommended posture and should be dropped from
it -- keeping a knob that cannot act is exactly the armed-but-inert failure standing
invariant #4 exists to forbid.  Its lasting value is then the per-station offset
DIAGNOSTIC, not the reframe.
